questions.prompt: What is the chapter's main claim about feeds?
choices: They are next-item sequences with weak stopping cues that easily outlast prior intent
They are harmless as long as each post is short
They are exactly the same as reading one article

explanation.gentle: The problem is the stream's continuation logic, not just one post.
explanation.direct: Feeds are sequence environments that keep supplying the next item.

questions.prompt: Why can feed drift feel small while becoming serious?
choices: Because many tiny swipes and refreshes accumulate into a long session
Because one post always contains all the harm by itself
Because feeds automatically become useful after enough time

explanation.gentle: The drift hides inside lots of little permissions.
explanation.direct: Accumulation is the mechanism to notice.

questions.prompt: What stronger correction does the chapter recommend?
choices: Treat feeds as bounded retrieval with a purpose and a stopping rule
Open feeds more often so they feel less tempting
Stay in the stream until it feels naturally finished

explanation.gentle: The chapter wants borders around entry and exit.
explanation.direct: Purpose and stopping rules beat ambient wandering.
explanation.competitive: Get on with a ticket and get off on schedule.

questions.prompt: What makes feeds different from online articles in the previous chapter?
choices: Feeds keep supplying the next item without a stable boundary around one chosen object
Feeds never contain anything useful
Articles have no links or recommendations

explanation.gentle: The article chapter focused on one reading task spreading outward; this one focuses on endless succession.
explanation.direct: A feed is a stream, not one bounded piece to finish.
explanation.competitive: The launchpad became a conveyor belt.

questions.prompt: Why is refresh behavior important in this chapter?
choices: Because refresh keeps reopening the sequence with new novelty before closure arrives
Because refresh automatically improves focus
Because refresh is only a smartphone hardware issue

explanation.gentle: Refresh gives the stream another chance to continue.
explanation.direct: It extends the session by renewing novelty.
explanation.competitive: The belt keeps calling in reinforcements.

questions.prompt: A student checks a class discussion feed for one answer and keeps scrolling unrelated posts. What is the stronger correction?
choices: Take the needed answer and leave instead of letting the stream become the study session
Assume unrelated posts will eventually help the assignment
Stay until the feed runs out on its own

explanation.gentle: The original task should regain control.
explanation.competitive: Take the note and leave the carnival.

questions.prompt: What limit does the chapter preserve?
choices: Useful material can appear in feeds even though the sequence design is still destabilizing
All feed content is worthless
Feeds can only be fixed by deleting the internet

explanation.gentle: The chapter stays honest about why people return to feeds.
explanation.direct: Value can exist inside a structure that still overextends contact.
explanation.competitive: Gold can appear in a river without making drowning smart.

questions.prompt: What kind of relationship does the chapter reject?
choices: An always-open relationship to the feed where novelty decides when the session ends
A deliberate check for one update
A scheduled retrieval block with a stopping point

explanation.gentle: The problem is ambient, unbounded staying.
explanation.direct: The chapter rejects open-ended wandering governed by the stream itself.
explanation.competitive: Do not let the belt name the adjournment.

questions.prompt: How does the chapter suggest reducing feed power before you even open it?
choices: Reduce default exposure so feeds do not greet you automatically all day
Keep every stream visible at all times
Rely only on remembering to resist in the moment

explanation.gentle: Default exposure shapes how often the stream gets a vote.
explanation.direct: Fewer feed surfaces make bounded use easier.
explanation.competitive: Do not let the belt set up in your hallway.

questions.prompt: Why does Chapter 20 come after feeds?
choices: Because repeated losses to endless sequence can require future-facing constraints set in advance
Because precommitments are only for paper planners
Because feed problems disappear once you notice them once

explanation.gentle: The next chapter answers what to do when live intention keeps losing.
explanation.direct: Precommitments matter when the stream repeatedly out-negotiates the present moment.
explanation.competitive: If the belt keeps winning, build the barricade first.
